AccessRestriction.name: AccessRestriction
AccessRestriction.description: An access restriction is a marking definition that describes a security, licensing, classification, operational security, or legal authority constraint on the use of a forensic tool capability. It is a subclass of uco-marking:MarkingDefinition because access restrictions are a specific form of data marking that conveys restrictions, permissions, and guidance for how capability data can be used and shared — the same semantic purpose served by UCO's marking namespace. By subclassing MarkingDefinition, access restrictions integrate into UCO's standard marking pipeline: they can be applied to any UcoObject via the objectMarking property, and they inherit the definitionType property which aligns with restrictionType. The toolcap-specific properties (restrictionType, restrictionLevel, restrictionDescription) provide forensic-domain refinement beyond what the base MarkingDefinition offers. When a specific investigative authorization is required, the restriction can link to a case-investigation:Authorization instance via requiredAuthorization. See https://www.nist.gov/publications for related information security marking standards.

properties.name: serialNumberObliterated

BenchmarkObservation.name: BenchmarkObservation
BenchmarkObservation.description: A benchmark observation is a single point-in-time record of testing a forensic tool's capability. It is a subclass of uco-core:Assertion because each observation is an empirical assertion about a tool's performance that is declared to be true by the benchmarking party. Each observation captures the results of one test run, including pass/fail outcome, completeness and accuracy metrics, standard information retrieval metrics (precision, recall, F1), confusion matrix counts (TP, FP, FN), processing performance, benchmark provenance (framework name, test case identifier, suite score), observable categories parsed or missed, tool and application versions tested, and the data format version. BenchmarkObservation instances are append-only: new test runs produce new instances rather than updating existing ones, preserving a full audit trail of capability evidence over time. The inherited uco-core:statement property from Assertion may carry a human-readable summary of the benchmark result. See https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.500-281 for the NIST CFTT benchmark methodology.

Block device nodes are used to apply access rights to the devices and to direct operations on the files to the appropriate device drivers. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_file_types]

CampaignCluster.name: CampaignCluster
CampaignCluster.description: An analytic partition of smishing messages produced by the SmishViz clustering pipeline (merged cluster label such as MC(5)). This is an ML-derived grouping for corpus analysis, not a confirmed adversary operation. See the SmishViz CASE/UCO repository (https://github.com/varnicm/smishviz-case-uco) and NIST SP 800-83 Rev. 1 guidance on analyzing malicious messaging campaigns (https://csrc.nist.gov/publications/detail/sp/800-83/rev-1/final).

Capability.name: Capability
Capability.description: A capability is the ability of an entity to perform some action or produce some result. Capabilities are connected to their possessors (tools, modules, parsers, people, organizations) via uco-core:Relationship instances with kindOfRelationship='hasCapability'. A capability may be described unstructured (via name/description) or structured (via structuredCharacterization pointing to an ActionPattern). See https://github.com/ucoProject/UCO/issues/596 for related Software hierarchy work.

properties.name: cellSiteLocationAreaCode

properties.name: cellSiteNetworkCode
properties.description: This code identifies the mobile operator of the cell site. For GSM, this is the Mobile Network Code (MNC) and for CMDA this is the network identifier (NID).

properties.name: cellSiteType
properties.description: Specifies the technology used by the Cell Site (e.g., GSM, CDMA, or LTE).

CharacterDeviceNode.name: CharacterDeviceNode
CharacterDeviceNode.description: A character device node is a UNIX filesystem special file that serves as a conduit to communicate with devices, providing only a serial stream of input or accepting a serial stream of output. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_file_types]

CoercionCycle.name: CoercionCycle
CoercionCycle.description: Self-sustaining sextortion loop in which retained imagery becomes perpetual leverage: the offender redeploys the same retained material to demand new content, extending leverage further without acquiring new initial leverage. Structurally distinct from a single threat-delivery event; the cycle has no natural termination except apprehension or removal of material. Modeled as a complex exploitation event (occurrent) rather than a situation, because gUFO declares events and situations disjoint; the persisting leverage state is carried by the retained artifact via sustainedBy.

properties.name: coercionCycleDemandType
properties.description: Type of demand driving a coercion cycle iteration (imagery_quota, live_conduct, financial, victim_recruitment).

properties.name: cyclesBetween
properties.description: Phase instances that form the coercion loop (typically threat delivery and exploitation phases in sextortion, or equivalent phase nodes in other offense trajectories).

properties.name: sustainedBy
properties.description: Retained material or artifact that powers the coercion cycle (e.g., intimate images retained from prior exploitation).

properties.name: terminationCondition
properties.description: How the coercion cycle ended if known (apprehension, material_removal, victim_ceased_response, unknown).

CoercionLeverage.name: CoercionLeverage
CoercionLeverage.description: Platform affordance that amplifies coercive leverage (screenshots, forwarding, contact export, payment rails).

properties.name: substanceName

ConvictionRecord.name: ConvictionRecord
ConvictionRecord.description: A durable record that a person was convicted of one or more criminal charges (e.g., by jury verdict, bench trial, or plea agreement). Used for current-case dispositions and for limited prior-conviction history relevant to charging or sentencing. Trauma-informed modeling: store only structured legal facts needed for interoperability; do not encode graphic offense narrative in this class. Modeled as gUFO Object.

properties.name: chargeCount
properties.description: The total number of criminal charges associated with a ConvictionRecord or LegalProceeding (aggregate total, not the ordinal of a single count). Constrained on ConvictionRecord by ConvictionRecordShape (minInclusive 1, maxInclusive 100). Distinct from countNumber, which is the ordinal count number within a charging instrument. NOTE: some existing example graphs historically used chargeCount on individual CriminalCharge nodes as an ordinal; that usage SHOULD migrate to countNumber in a follow-up (this declaration does not rewrite those examples).

properties.name: convictionDate
properties.description: Date and time when the conviction was entered (verdict, acceptance of plea, or equivalent disposition). Required by ConvictionRecordShape as xsd:dateTime.

properties.name: convictionType
properties.description: How the conviction was obtained. Allowed values (ConvictionRecordShape): jury_verdict, bench_trial, plea_agreement, default_judgment, summary_conviction.

properties.name: priorConvictions
properties.description: Number of prior criminal convictions associated with the subject of this ConvictionRecord (aggregate count for history context; 0–50 per ConvictionRecordShape). Use non-graphic, structured counts only.

properties.description: Links a criminal charge to the charging instrument (complaint, indictment, superseding indictment, information) in which it is asserted.

properties.name: chargeClassification
properties.description: The offense classification in the governing jurisdiction, e.g. 'Class A Felony' per 18 U.S.C. § 3559 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/3559).

properties.name: chargeDisposition
properties.description: The current disposition of the charge, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'pending', 'dismissed', 'acquitted', 'convicted-by-verdict', 'convicted-by-plea', 'merged'.

properties.name: countLabel
properties.description: The count designation as printed in the charging instrument, e.g. 'Count 1', 'Counts 4-10', 'Count 1sss' (PACER superseding-indictment notation).

properties.name: countNumber
properties.description: Ordinal count number of the charge within its charging instrument. A charge asserted in a range of counts (e.g. Counts 4-10) may carry multiple values.

properties.name: objectOffense
properties.description: Links an inchoate or derivative criminal charge (conspiracy, attempt, solicitation, aiding-abetting, predicate-linked offense) to the charge representing its object or predicate offense, e.g. a conspiracy-to-murder count to the murder offense conspired at, or an 18 U.S.C. § 924(c) firearm count to the crime-of-violence count it is charged in furtherance of.

properties.name: offenseForm
properties.description: The form of the charged offense, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'substantive' (completed offense), 'conspiracy' (agreement to commit an object offense, e.g. 18 U.S.C. §§ 371, 1117), 'attempt' (e.g. 18 U.S.C. § 1113), 'solicitation', 'aiding-abetting' (e.g. 18 U.S.C. § 2), 'derivative' (offense defined by reference to a predicate offense, e.g. 18 U.S.C. § 924(c) use of a firearm in furtherance of a crime of violence). Use objectOffense to link a non-substantive charge to its object or predicate charge.

properties.name: statuteCitation
properties.description: Citation of the charged offense in the governing jurisdiction, e.g. '18 U.S.C. §§ 1117 & 1114'.

CrowdsourcingInvestigation.description: Investigation leveraging public participation for object identification, geolocation, and evidence analysis. Modeled as gUFO Event.

CryptocurrencyAddressFacet.name: CryptocurrencyAddressFacet
CryptocurrencyAddressFacet.description: A cryptocurrency address facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a blockchain address used to send and receive virtual assets on a distributed ledger network. A virtual currency address is roughly equivalent to an anonymous account number and has a corresponding private key needed to spend value held at the address (see the affidavit in United States v. Lichtenstein, No. 1:23-cr-00239-CKK (D.D.C.), Statement of Facts nn.4-9, and the INTERPOL DW-VA Taxonomy entity 'wallet': https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#wallet). Attach to a uco-observable:ObservableObject via uco-core:hasFacet.

properties.name: addressFormat
properties.description: The encoding format of the address as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'Base58Check', 'Bech32', 'Hex'. See BIP-173 (https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0173.mediawiki) for Bech32 and https://en.bitcoin.it/wiki/Base58Check_encoding for Base58Check.

properties.name: addressValue
properties.description: The cryptocurrency address string, e.g. '1CGA4s...' (Base58Check), 'bc1q...' (Bech32), or '0x8CE693CB0626924583931F25f50AF8fC1C6517F0' (Ethereum hex). See Bitcoin address encodings in BIP-173 (https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0173.mediawiki).

properties.name: blockchainNetwork
properties.description: The distributed ledger network the address or transaction belongs to, e.g. 'Bitcoin Mainnet', 'Ethereum', 'Litecoin'. A blockchain is a public transaction ledger that includes a record of every transaction that has ever occurred on the network (https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#blockchain).

properties.name: cryptocurrencyType
properties.description: The type of cryptocurrency, as an open vocabulary of ticker symbols. Recommended values: BTC, ETH, LTC, XMR, ZEC, DASH, ETC, BCH, BSV, BTG, XRP, DOGE, SOL, ADA, DOT, AVAX, MATIC, USDT, USDC, WETH. Producers may use identifiers not in this list to accommodate new virtual assets (ticker symbols as listed by major data providers, e.g. https://coinmarketcap.com/).

CryptocurrencyMixingService.name: CryptocurrencyMixingService
CryptocurrencyMixingService.description: A cryptocurrency mixing service (mixer or tumbler) obscures the link between transaction inputs and outputs by combining or shuffling the virtual assets of multiple users — for example via coinjoin, a method where two or more user transactions are combined into a single blockchain transaction with multiple inputs and outputs (INTERPOL DW-VA Taxonomy: https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#coinjoin). Examples cited in federal prosecutions include Bitcoin Fog, Helix, and ChipMixer (United States v. Lichtenstein, No. 1:23-cr-00239-CKK (D.D.C.), Statement of the Offense para. 19; see also FinCEN guidance FIN-2019-G001, https://www.fincen.gov/resources/statutes-and-regulations/guidance).

CryptocurrencyTransactionFacet.name: CryptocurrencyTransactionFacet
CryptocurrencyTransactionFacet.description: A cryptocurrency transaction facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a transfer of value recorded on a blockchain distributed ledger. Attach to a uco-observable:ObservableObject representing the transaction; model the source and destination addresses as uco-observable:ObservableRelationship instances with uco-core:kindOfRelationship values 'Transaction_Input' and 'Transaction_Output' and a cryptoinv:transferAmount. This pattern natively supports UTXO-chain transactions (Bitcoin) with multiple inputs and outputs (see https://developer.bitcoin.org/devguide/transactions.html) as well as account-based chains (Ethereum).

properties.name: blockHash
properties.description: The hash of the block containing this transaction (https://developer.bitcoin.org/reference/block_chain.html).

properties.name: blockNumber
properties.description: The block number (block height) in the blockchain at which the transaction was confirmed (https://developer.bitcoin.org/reference/block_chain.html).

properties.name: confirmationCount
properties.description: The number of blockchain confirmations at the time of observation. This is a point-in-time snapshot, not a time-varying quality (time-varying properties are deferred to https://github.com/ucoProject/UCO/issues/535).

properties.name: transactionFee
properties.description: The transaction fee in the native cryptocurrency unit of the network (https://developer.bitcoin.org/devguide/transactions.html#transaction-fees-and-change). Also used on cryptoinv:VirtualAssetLedgerRecordFacet when a VASP reports a network or platform fee on a ledger row.

properties.name: transactionHash
properties.description: The unique hash identifier of the blockchain transaction, e.g. '6e0d701ac2ea3ad87fc8bcaa786b994aa943f5eb9a67a1e345769bb090bf5b9e' (a Bitcoin transaction identifier / txid; see https://developer.bitcoin.org/reference/transactions.html).

properties.name: transactionStatus
properties.description: The status of the transaction or ledger row at the time of observation, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'Confirmed', 'Pending', 'Failed'. Used on cryptoinv:CryptocurrencyTransactionFacet and cryptoinv:VirtualAssetLedgerRecordFacet.

properties.name: transactionType
properties.description: The investigative characterization of the transaction, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'Transfer', 'Exchange', 'Purchase', 'Mixing', 'Withdrawal', 'Deposit', 'ContractExecution', 'Staking', 'Unstaking'. Mixing and chain-hopping transaction types are defined in the INTERPOL DW-VA Taxonomy (https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#coinjoin).

CryptocurrencyWalletFacet.name: CryptocurrencyWalletFacet
CryptocurrencyWalletFacet.description: A cryptocurrency wallet facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a wallet: software, a device, or a hosted service that keeps track of the private keys used to sign virtual-asset transactions, and which may contain many virtual currency addresses (INTERPOL DW-VA Taxonomy: https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#wallet). First proposed as CryptoWalletFacet in https://github.com/casework/CASE/issues/87; this revision omits time-varying balance properties, which remain blocked by https://github.com/ucoProject/UCO/issues/535 — use cryptoinv:VirtualAssetHoldingFacet for point-in-time holdings snapshots.

properties.name: addressCount
properties.description: The number of virtual currency addresses contained in the wallet at the time of observation (a wallet may include many addresses, each with a corresponding private key).

properties.name: hostedWalletCompartment
properties.description: The provider-hosted wallet compartment reported by a VASP, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values observed on exchange legal returns: 'Spot', 'Funding', 'Earn', 'Futures', 'Margin', 'Card'. A hosted wallet is one where a third party retains the customer's funds (INTERPOL DW-VA Taxonomy: https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#hosted-wallet). This is a ledger partition, not proof of on-chain control.

properties.name: walletIdentifier
properties.description: An investigative identifier for the wallet or address cluster, e.g. the first characters of a representative address ('Wallet 1CGA4s') or a chain-analysis cluster label ('Cluster 36B6mu'). A cluster is a grouping of addresses believed to be contained within a single wallet (United States v. Lichtenstein, No. 1:23-cr-00239-CKK (D.D.C.), Statement of Facts n.28).

properties.name: walletType
properties.description: The custody model and form factor of the wallet, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'hosted' (a third party retains the customer's funds: https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#hosted-wallet), 'unhosted' (the user exercises total, independent control over funds: https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#unhosted-wallet), 'hardware' (https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#hardware_wallet), 'software' (https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#software_wallet), 'paper'.

properties.name: providesAccessTo
properties.description:
The storage medium that this device interface gives access to.

The interface is a way of reaching the medium, not the medium itself, so the
medium's characteristics (model, serial number, capacity) are stated on the
StorageMedium through its DeviceFacet and StorageMediumFacet, not on the
interface. The same medium can be reached through a write-protected interface
on one occasion and a read-write one on another. A hardware write blocker used
to create the interface is a separate uco-observable:WriteBlocker, which is
itself a Device, and is never the value of this property.

A uco-observable:Disk is not a Device in UCO 1.5.0. UCO asks for a Disk node to
carry the additional type uco-observable:StorageMedium in preparation for UCO
2.0.0, and a Disk typed that way is a valid value here.

DisclosureObligation.name: DisclosureObligation
DisclosureObligation.description: A prosecutor's sourced duty to disclose specified information or evidence to the defense. Use disclosureKind to record the governing doctrine (Brady, Giglio, Jencks, or Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 16) and disclosureStatus for the current production state. Do not infer an obligation from the mere existence of exam notes or statements. See Brady v. Maryland, 373 U.S. 83 (1963) (https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/373/83/), Giglio v. United States, 405 U.S. 150 (1972) (https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/405/150/), the Jencks Act, 18 U.S.C. § 3500 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/3500), and Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 16 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/rules/frcrmp/rule_16).

EnterpriseRole@ext.rico.rico.name: EnterpriseRole
EnterpriseRole@ext.rico.rico.description: An enterprise role is a functional position or division-of-labor responsibility that a member or associate serves within a racketeering enterprise, as alleged in a charging instrument — for example organizer, target identifier, caller (social engineer), money launderer, database hacker, or residential burglar (see the roles alleged in United States v. Lam et al., No. 1:24-cr-00417-CKK (D.D.C.), Second Superseding Indictment ¶¶ 25-32). Link a person to the role with a uco-core:Relationship of kind 'Has_Role' and the role to the enterprise with a uco-core:Relationship of kind 'Role_Within'; one person may fulfill several roles and one role may be fulfilled by several persons.

properties.name: assertedIn
properties.description: Links a criminal charge to the charging instrument (complaint, indictment, superseding indictment, information) in which it is asserted.

properties.name: chargeClassification
properties.description: The offense classification in the governing jurisdiction, e.g. 'Class A Felony' per 18 U.S.C. § 3559 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/3559).

properties.name: chargeDisposition
properties.description: The current disposition of the charge, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'pending', 'dismissed', 'acquitted', 'convicted-by-verdict', 'convicted-by-plea', 'merged'.

properties.name: countLabel
properties.description: The count designation as printed in the charging instrument, e.g. 'Count 1', 'Counts 4-10', 'Count 1sss' (PACER superseding-indictment notation).

properties.name: countNumber
properties.description: Ordinal count number of the charge within its charging instrument. A charge asserted in a range of counts (e.g. Counts 4-10) may carry multiple values.

properties.name: objectOffense
properties.description: Links an inchoate or derivative criminal charge (conspiracy, attempt, solicitation, aiding-abetting, predicate-linked offense) to the charge representing its object or predicate offense, e.g. a conspiracy-to-murder count to the murder offense conspired at, or an 18 U.S.C. § 924(c) firearm count to the crime-of-violence count it is charged in furtherance of.

properties.name: offenseForm
properties.description: The form of the charged offense, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'substantive' (completed offense), 'conspiracy' (agreement to commit an object offense, e.g. 18 U.S.C. §§ 371, 1117), 'attempt' (e.g. 18 U.S.C. § 1113), 'solicitation', 'aiding-abetting' (e.g. 18 U.S.C. § 2), 'derivative' (offense defined by reference to a predicate offense, e.g. 18 U.S.C. § 924(c) use of a firearm in furtherance of a crime of violence). Use objectOffense to link a non-substantive charge to its object or predicate charge.

properties.name: statuteCitation
properties.description: Citation of the charged offense in the governing jurisdiction, e.g. '18 U.S.C. §§ 1117 & 1114'.

properties.name: jurisdictionKind
properties.description: Whether a charge or proceeding is state, federal, or unknown from the source. Closed vocabulary: 'state', 'federal', 'unknown'. Use 'unknown' only when the source does not establish jurisdiction; do not infer jurisdiction from a URL host or agency label.

Flight.name: Flight
Flight.description: A flight is a single sortie of an unmanned aircraft, bounded by the transitions that make it airworthy and inert again — typically motor arming and disarming. Use the inherited uco-core:startTime and uco-core:endTime for those bounds, uas:takeoffLocation for the launch point the autopilot recorded, and uas:flightTrack to reach the ordered position fixes. A log file may contain several flights; model each as its own instance so that per-sortie findings do not bleed across them.

properties.description: The ordered sequence of position fixes flown during this flight, as a uco-observable:GeoLocationTrack whose entries are uco-observable:GeoLocationEntry instances.

properties.name: maximumAltitudeAboveTakeoff
properties.description: The greatest altitude reached during the flight relative to the takeoff point, in metres. Stated relative to takeoff because that is the datum most aviation rules use (for example the 400 ft above-ground limit in 14 CFR 107.51) and the one autopilots compute directly; an above-mean-sea-level figure for the same instant belongs on the position fix, qualified with an altitude reference.

properties.name: takeoffLocation
properties.description: The launch point of the flight as the autopilot recorded it — for ArduPilot, the EKF origin and home position captured at arming. This is the aircraft's own belief about where it started, which is evidence in its own right and may differ from where it actually started if the position solution was spoofed or degraded.

FlightLog.name: FlightLog
FlightLog.description: A flight log is a log written by an unmanned aircraft's autopilot or by a ground control station, recording telemetry, state transitions, operator commands and text messages for one or more sorties. Examples: ArduPilot DataFlash logs (.BIN) written onboard, MAVLink telemetry logs (.tlog) written by the ground station, PX4 ULog (.ulg), and DJI TXT/DAT flight records. Use uas:logFormat to record which, and attach uco-observable:FileFacet plus uco-observable:ContentDataFacet for the container and its hash. Individual rows are uco-observable:EventRecord instances related to this log.

FlightModeChange.name: FlightModeChange
FlightModeChange.description: A flight mode change is a transition of the autopilot from one flight mode to another — for example from a pilot-commanded mode to a return-to-launch or landing mode. The forensically decisive part is not the destination mode but the authority behind it: uas:flightModeChangeReason distinguishes a stick input from a ground-station command from an autonomous failsafe, and uas:commandedBy names the control-link endpoint that issued it when the log identifies one. Attributing an unexpected mode change is the central question in most drone incident investigations.

properties.name: autopilotFamily
properties.description: The autopilot firmware family whose vocabulary the recorded mode and reason strings belong to, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'ArduPilot', 'PX4', 'DJI', 'Autel', 'Betaflight', 'INAV'. Without it, a bare mode string such as 'AUTO' is not interpretable.

properties.name: flightMode
properties.description: The autopilot flight mode entered, as the vendor names it and kept verbatim — for example 'GUIDED', 'RTL', 'LOITER', 'AUTO' (ArduPilot); 'Position', 'Return' (PX4). Do not normalise across vendors: the same label can mean different behaviour on different firmware, and the mapping belongs in analysis, not ingest.

properties.name: flightModeChangeReason
properties.description: Why the autopilot changed mode, kept as the vendor's own reason string where one exists (ArduPilot logs a ModeReason with every MODE record; PX4 records a navigation state change source). This is the property that separates an operator decision from an autonomous failsafe from a remote command: 'RC_COMMAND' means a stick input, 'GCS_COMMAND' means a ground-station command arrived over the control link, and the various failsafe reasons mean the aircraft decided for itself. Where the firmware supplies no reason, leave unset rather than inferring one.

properties.name: previousFlightMode
properties.description: The flight mode the autopilot was in immediately before this change, using the same vendor vocabulary as uas:flightMode. Assert it only when the log or a prior record establishes it.

A forfeiture money judgment for a sum equal to the value of the property involved may accompany the forfeiture of specific property.

HypothesisedRecord.name: HypothesisedRecord
HypothesisedRecord.description: A database record hypothesised to have existed, typically reconstructed from deallocated or partially overwritten storage such as freeblocks, unallocated page space, or freelist pages. The claim it makes is one of extent: that these bytes constituted one record, beginning and ending where the reconstruction says. That claim can fail - a sequence of ordinary integers can decode as a plausible record header, adjacent deletions can merge into one freeblock, and a later write can overwrite the leading bytes - so a HypothesisedRecord is deliberately not a solveit-observable:SQLiteRecord. Decoded values are linked with solveit-analysis:hasField, and the page the bytes came from with solveit-observable:recoveredFromPage. Which table the record belonged to is a separate claim, and is not asserted here: it is made by a solveit-analysis:HypothesisedTableAttribution, so that one reconstruction can carry several competing attributions without being duplicated.

HypothesisedRelationship.name: HypothesisedRelationship
HypothesisedRelationship.description: A relationship between entities that is hypothesised to exist. This covers inferred associations between persons, accounts, devices or locations - drawn from co-occurrence patterns, shared identifiers, or behavioural analysis - and also structural claims such as attributing a recovered database record to the table it belonged to. Being a uco-core:Relationship, the entities are named with uco-core:source and uco-core:target and the nature of the claim with uco-core:kindOfRelationship. What is uncertain is the relationship, not the entities: source and target may both be perfectly ordinary observed objects.

HypothesisedTableAttribution.name: HypothesisedTableAttribution
HypothesisedTableAttribution.description: The claim that a recovered record belonged to a particular table. The record is the uco-core:source and the table the uco-core:target; neither is itself in doubt, only the link between them. Attribution rests on different grounds in different cases - a record recovered from a freeblock sits on a page owned by a known table, whereas one recovered from a freelist page has lost that context and can only be matched by column shape. Where several tables are possible, one HypothesisedTableAttribution is made per candidate and they are collected in a solveit-analysis:HypothesisSet as mutually exclusive alternatives.

properties.name: modifiedTime
properties.description: Specifies the time that this particular version of the object was modified. The object creator can use the time it deems most appropriate as the time this version of the object was modified. The value of the modified property for a given object version MUST be later than or equal to the value of the created property. Object creators MUST update the modified property when creating a new version of an object. The modified timestamp MUST be precise to the nearest millisecond (exactly three digits after the decimal place in seconds).

Laptop.name: Laptop
Laptop.description: A laptop, laptop computer, or notebook computer is a small, portable personal computer with a screen and alphanumeric keyboard. These typically have a clam shell form factor with the screen mounted on the inside of the upper lid and the keyboard on the inside of the lower lid, although 2-in-1 PCs with a detachable keyboard are often marketed as laptops or as having a laptop mode. properties.name: providesAccessTo
properties.description:
The storage medium that this device interface gives access to.

The interface is a way of reaching the medium, not the medium itself, so the
medium's characteristics (model, serial number, capacity) are stated on the
StorageMedium through its DeviceFacet and StorageMediumFacet, not on the
interface. The same medium can be reached through a write-protected interface
on one occasion and a read-write one on another. A hardware write blocker used
to create the interface is a separate uco-observable:WriteBlocker, which is
itself a Device, and is never the value of this property.

A uco-observable:Disk is not a Device in UCO 1.5.0. UCO asks for a Disk node to
carry the additional type uco-observable:StorageMedium in preparation for UCO
2.0.0, and a Disk typed that way is a valid value here.

MavlinkEndpointFacet.name: MavlinkEndpointFacet
MavlinkEndpointFacet.description: A MAVLink endpoint facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a node addressable on a MAVLink control link, identified by the (system id, component id) pair that every MAVLink frame carries. Attach it to whichever observable plays the role — the aircraft itself, a ground control station, a companion computer, or an unattributed node observed only as a source address in the log. Because MAVLink v1 and v2 carry no authentication by default, the system id is an assertion by the sender and not proof of identity; record uas:senderAuthenticationEnforced so a reader can tell how much weight the address bears.

properties.name: authorizedGroundControlStationId
properties.description: The MAVLink system id that the autopilot was configured to accept as its ground control station — ArduPilot's SYSID_MYGCS parameter, or the equivalent on other firmware. Comparing it with the system ids actually observed on the link is the basic test for whether commands came from the expected station.

properties.name: mavlinkComponentId
properties.description: The MAVLink component id carried in every frame this endpoint sends, distinguishing components within one system per the MAV_COMPONENT enumeration — for example 1 (autopilot), 190 (Mission Planner ground station), 191 (QGroundControl), 240 (peripheral).

properties.name: mavlinkComponentName
properties.description: The MAV_COMPONENT enumeration name for the component id, recorded alongside the number so the graph is readable without a lookup table — for example 'MAV_COMP_ID_AUTOPILOT1', 'MAV_COMP_ID_MISSIONPLANNER'.

properties.name: mavlinkDialect
properties.description: The MAVLink dialect and wire version the endpoint speaks, kept verbatim — for example 'ardupilotmega v2.0', 'common v1.0'. The dialect determines which message identifiers decode to which semantics, so a parse is only reproducible if it is recorded.

properties.name: mavlinkSystemId
properties.description: The MAVLink system id carried in every frame this endpoint sends. It addresses a vehicle or a ground station on the link. The wire field is 8-bit, so the shape admits 0-255 and recovered or partial logs validate, but 0 is reserved for broadcast and a well-formed sender therefore uses 1-255. It is self-asserted by the sender and, unless message signing is in use, trivially forgeable; treat an unexpected system id as an observation about the link, not as an identification of an operator.

properties.name: senderAuthenticationEnforced
properties.description: Whether the autopilot was configured to reject commands whose source did not match its authorised ground control station — ArduPilot's SYSID_ENFORCE parameter, or an equivalent such as MAVLink 2 message signing. When false, any node that can reach the radio link can command the aircraft, and the system id in the log is an unverified claim. Recording this is what lets a later reader judge how much an observed sender address proves.

properties.name: establishedForWeakness
properties.description: The weaknesses this capability was established against. One mitigation typically addresses many weaknesses, and a capability that names only its mitigation is read as covering all of them, including the ones the publisher never tested. Naming weaknesses here records what was actually established rather than what the mitigation could in principle address. There is no minimum: a capability naming no weakness declares no weakness scope and keeps the meaning it was published with, because every profile published before this term existed carries none.

properties.name: supportingCitation
properties.description: Evidence for this capability - a test report, a validation study, a published paper. The idiom here is that the profile mints its own Citation, carrying solveit-core:citationPlaintext or solveit-core:citationBibtex and omitting solveit-core:citationID, so a publisher can cite their own test report without it being registered in the DFCite series and the profile depends on nothing outside itself. This departs from the comment on solveit-core:Citation, which describes a registry reference reached from a Technique, Weakness or Mitigation. The departure is recorded here rather than reconciled there, because widening a core term to serve one module would put the change in the module that did not need it.

properties.name: statement
properties.description: A textual statement of an assertion.

properties.name: assertsState
properties.description: The state this observed assertion claims was occupied.

properties.name: atInterval
properties.description: owl-time ProperInterval during which the asserted state occupancy held. Type is SHACL-only (sh:class time:ProperInterval); no rdfs:range, so the class check is non-vacuous under RDFS entailment. See https://www.w3.org/TR/owl-time/#time:ProperInterval.

properties.name: isTerminal
properties.description: Marks this PhaseAssertion as the terminal (final observed) occupancy in its traj:Trajectory. When true, traj:terminalPolarity must also be asserted to type the realized outcome. A single-path Trajectory carries exactly one PhaseAssertion with isTerminal true; this property does not itself model or require a branch to a second outcome.

properties.name: sequenceIndex
properties.description: Zero-based (or one-based, consistently per graph) order of this PhaseAssertion within its Trajectory. Prefer this over rdf:List for SPARQL/SHACL usability. SHACL enforces uniqueness of sequenceIndex within a Trajectory; consecutive/dense numbering and a required zero- vs one-based origin are not enforced.

properties.name: terminalPolarity
properties.description: Controlled-vocabulary outcome type for a terminal traj:PhaseAssertion (traj:isTerminal true). Current vocabulary: 'completed' (the modeled chain reached its endpoint — later arrest/prosecution of the offender does not convert a finished chain into 'disrupted') and 'disrupted' (an intervention ended the trajectory mid-chain, before the modeled endpoint was reached). Modeled as an open xsd:string constrained by SHACL sh:in — not a traj:State subclass — so additional outcome types can be added without a T-Box change. Asserting this property on a single-path Trajectory's one terminal PhaseAssertion does not imply or require instantiating a second, opposite-polarity branch anywhere in the same Trajectory.

PhaseConsistency.name: PhaseConsistency
PhaseConsistency.description: Validation ensuring phase modeling follows gUFO intrinsic constraints and proper transition semantics.

PhaseTransitionEvent.name: PhaseTransitionEvent
PhaseTransitionEvent.description: Event marking transition between investigation phases. Modeled as gUFO Event with temporal boundaries and phase change effects.

properties.name: outcomeScope
properties.description: Whether a charge, plea, verdict, sentence, conviction, or potential penalty belongs to the current matter or to prior-conviction history mentioned by the source. Closed vocabulary: 'current-case', 'prior-history'. Required for independently queryable current versus prior outcomes. See Federal Rule of Evidence 404(b) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/rules/fre/rule_404) for the prior-act distinction this property encodes.

properties.name: pleaType
properties.description: The type of plea entered, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'guilty', 'not-guilty', 'nolo-contendere'.

PleaAgreement.name: PleaAgreement
PleaAgreement.description: A plea agreement is a negotiated agreement under Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 11(c) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/rules/frcrmp/rule_11) in which a defendant agrees to plead guilty to one or more charges, typically in exchange for concessions such as dismissal of other charges, a sentencing recommendation, or non-prosecution commitments. This class models the legal instrument and its terms; model the underlying court-filed document separately as a uco-observable:ObservableObject with a uco-observable:FileFacet and link the two with a uco-core:Relationship.

PleaAgreement@ext.legalproc.legalproc.name: PleaAgreement
PleaAgreement@ext.legalproc.legalproc.description: A plea agreement is a negotiated agreement between the prosecution and a defendant concerning the plea that will be entered and any agreed dispositions or sentencing recommendations, as recognized by Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 11(c) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/rules/frcrmp/rule_11). The plea itself remains a separate Plea resource linked by recordsPlea. This class is the jurisdiction-neutral plea-agreement concept for CASE/UCO graphs; do not use domain-specific homonyms such as cryptoinv:PleaAgreement.

ProcessThread.name: ProcessThread
ProcessThread.description: A process thread is the smallest sequence of programmed instructions that can be managed independently by a scheduler on a computer, which is typically a part of the operating system. It is a component of a process. Multiple threads can exist within one process, executing concurrently and sharing resources such as memory, while different processes do not share these resources. In particular, the threads of a process share its executable code and the values of its dynamically allocated variables and non-thread-local global variables at any given time. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thread_(computing)]

RacketeeringEnterprise.name: RacketeeringEnterprise
RacketeeringEnterprise.description: A racketeering enterprise is an 'enterprise' as defined in 18 U.S.C. § 1961(4) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/1961): any individual, partnership, corporation, association, or other legal entity, and any union or group of individuals associated in fact although not a legal entity, whose affairs are conducted or participated in through a pattern of racketeering activity (18 U.S.C. § 1962, https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/1962). An association-in-fact enterprise must have a purpose, relationships among those associated with the enterprise, and longevity sufficient to permit the associates to pursue the enterprise's purpose (Boyle v. United States, 556 U.S. 938 (2009), https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/556/938/). Record the charged purposes and the interstate/foreign commerce nexus in uco-core:description; record membership with uco-core:Relationship nodes of kind 'Member_Of' from persons to the enterprise; record the charged operating span with existence-interval or description conventions.

properties.name: providesAccessTo
properties.description:
The storage medium that this device interface gives access to.

The interface is a way of reaching the medium, not the medium itself, so the
medium's characteristics (model, serial number, capacity) are stated on the
StorageMedium through its DeviceFacet and StorageMediumFacet, not on the
interface. The same medium can be reached through a write-protected interface
on one occasion and a read-write one on another. A hardware write blocker used
to create the interface is a separate uco-observable:WriteBlocker, which is
itself a Device, and is never the value of this property.

A uco-observable:Disk is not a Device in UCO 1.5.0. UCO asks for a Disk node to
carry the additional type uco-observable:StorageMedium in preparation for UCO
2.0.0, and a Disk typed that way is a valid value here.

ReparsePoint.name: ReparsePoint
ReparsePoint.description: A reparse point is a type of NTFS (New Technology File System) object which is an optional attribute of files and directories meant to define some sort of preprocessing before accessing the said file or directory. For instance reparse points can be used to redirect access to files which have been moved to long term storage so that some application would retrieve them and make them directly accessible. A reparse point contains a reparse tag and data that are interpreted by a filesystem filter identified by the tag. [based on https://jp-andre.pagesperso-orange.fr/junctions.html ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NTFS_reparse_point]

Sentence.name: Sentence
Sentence.description: A sentence is a penalty recommended by a party or imposed by a tribunal upon conviction of a criminal charge. Use sentenceKind to record the kind of imposed or recommended sentence (custodial term, supervised release, probation, community service, or a fine imposed as part of the sentence). Do not use this class for bail, bond, pretrial detention conditions, restitution, forfeiture, special assessments, statutory maxima, guideline ranges, or other potential penalties; those facts use PretrialReleaseCondition, RestitutionOrder, ForfeitureOrder, or PotentialPenalty. See 18 U.S.C. § 3553 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/3553).

properties.name: outcomeScope
properties.description: Whether a charge, plea, verdict, sentence, conviction, or potential penalty belongs to the current matter or to prior-conviction history mentioned by the source. Closed vocabulary: 'current-case', 'prior-history'. Required for independently queryable current versus prior outcomes. See Federal Rule of Evidence 404(b) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/rules/fre/rule_404) for the prior-act distinction this property encodes.

properties.name: sentenceTerm

properties.name: assertedIn
properties.description: Links a criminal charge to the charging instrument (complaint, indictment, superseding indictment, information) in which it is asserted.

properties.name: chargeClassification
properties.description: The offense classification in the governing jurisdiction, e.g. 'Class A Felony' per 18 U.S.C. § 3559 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/3559).

properties.name: chargeDisposition
properties.description: The current disposition of the charge, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'pending', 'dismissed', 'acquitted', 'convicted-by-verdict', 'convicted-by-plea', 'merged'.

properties.name: countLabel
properties.description: The count designation as printed in the charging instrument, e.g. 'Count 1', 'Counts 4-10', 'Count 1sss' (PACER superseding-indictment notation).

properties.name: countNumber
properties.description: Ordinal count number of the charge within its charging instrument. A charge asserted in a range of counts (e.g. Counts 4-10) may carry multiple values.

properties.name: objectOffense
properties.description: Links an inchoate or derivative criminal charge (conspiracy, attempt, solicitation, aiding-abetting, predicate-linked offense) to the charge representing its object or predicate offense, e.g. a conspiracy-to-murder count to the murder offense conspired at, or an 18 U.S.C. § 924(c) firearm count to the crime-of-violence count it is charged in furtherance of.

properties.name: offenseForm
properties.description: The form of the charged offense, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'substantive' (completed offense), 'conspiracy' (agreement to commit an object offense, e.g. 18 U.S.C. §§ 371, 1117), 'attempt' (e.g. 18 U.S.C. § 1113), 'solicitation', 'aiding-abetting' (e.g. 18 U.S.C. § 2), 'derivative' (offense defined by reference to a predicate offense, e.g. 18 U.S.C. § 924(c) use of a firearm in furtherance of a crime of violence). Use objectOffense to link a non-substantive charge to its object or predicate charge.

properties.name: statuteCitation
properties.description: Citation of the charged offense in the governing jurisdiction, e.g. '18 U.S.C. §§ 1117 & 1114'.

properties.name: jurisdictionKind
properties.description: Whether a charge or proceeding is state, federal, or unknown from the source. Closed vocabulary: 'state', 'federal', 'unknown'. Use 'unknown' only when the source does not establish jurisdiction; do not infer jurisdiction from a URL host or agency label.

properties.description: Current status of the coordination (active, inactive, pending, completed, suspended, terminated).

properties.name: coordinationType
properties.description: Type of coordination (joint_investigation, parallel_investigation, information_sharing, resource_sharing, task_force_coordination, multi_agency_coordination).

properties.name: hasDataConsistency

properties.name: hasDataQuality

properties.name: hasSuccessRate

properties.name: hasValidationLevel
properties.description: Validation thoroughness (none, basic, standard, comprehensive, full_verification) - gUFO quality aspect.

properties.name: enactsAction
properties.description: The concrete uco-action:Action instance(s) that constitute this transition — distinct from traj:trigger (which may be any UcoObject the transition merely reacts to). Use traj:enactsAction when the transition IS an actor's action (typically typed with a domain technique class per the UCO 1.5.0 uco-action:Technique metaclass pattern), so the abused affordance can be carried on uco-action:instrument. Optional (no sh:minCount) and additive alongside traj:trigger; multiple values are allowed when a single directed edge is gated by co-occurring techniques (e.g. VoIP spoofing + fixed-script deployment on one transition). A bare-UcoObject-trigger Transition with no traj:enactsAction remains fully conformant.

properties.name: fromState
properties.description: Source state of a directed transition.

properties.name: guard
properties.description: Optional enabling condition on a transition, as an open-vocabulary string (e.g. analyst note or expression). Absent when the trigger alone is sufficient.

properties.name: toState
properties.description: Target state of a directed transition.

TransitionEstimate.name: TransitionEstimate
TransitionEstimate.description: An INFERRED estimate (probability or weight) for a traj:Transition, produced as part of a traj:StateMachineModel. Must carry prov:wasGeneratedBy and must not be typed as traj:PhaseAssertion.

UASFacet.name: UASFacet
UASFacet.description: A UAS facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the regulated identity and airframe configuration of an unmanned aircraft: the Remote ID broadcast under ASTM F3411, the civil aviation authority registration, the operator identifier, and the physical configuration that constrains how the aircraft can fly. Attach to a uas:UnmannedAircraft via uco-core:hasFacet.

properties.name: airframeConfiguration
properties.description: The physical motor and arm layout as the autopilot reports it, kept verbatim — for example 'QUAD/PLUS', 'QUAD/X', 'HEXA/X', 'OCTA/V'. Retain the vendor string rather than normalising it: the layout constrains achievable dynamics and is used when testing whether a claimed flight profile is physically possible.

properties.name: autopilotIdentifier
properties.description: The autopilot's own hardware or board identifier as recorded in the log or in the MAVLink AUTOPILOT_VERSION uid/uid2 field — for ArduPilot, the board UID written to the log at startup. It survives reflashing and parameter resets, so it links logs to a physical flight controller even when the airframe or registration changes.

properties.name: operatorId
properties.description: The operator identifier broadcast in the ASTM F3411 Operator ID message, which identifies the responsible operator rather than the airframe. Model the operator as a uco-identity:Identity and relate it to the aircraft with a uco-core:Relationship; this property records the raw broadcast value.

properties.name: registrationNumber
properties.description: The registration number issued by a civil aviation authority for this aircraft, kept verbatim including any prefix — for example an FAA registration under 14 CFR Part 48 or an EASA operator-linked registration.

properties.name: remoteIdSerialNumber
properties.description: The aircraft serial number broadcast as the ASTM F3411 Basic ID, formatted per ANSI/CTA-2063-A (manufacturer code, length code, then the manufacturer's serial). This is the identifier a Remote ID receiver observes over the air and the one that ties a broadcast to a registered airframe.

properties.name: remoteIdType
properties.description: Which ASTM F3411 UAS ID type the recorded identifier is, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'Serial Number' (ANSI/CTA-2063-A), 'CAA Registration ID', 'UTM Assigned UUID', 'Specific Session ID'. The type matters because only the serial number is durably bound to the airframe; session identifiers are deliberately ephemeral.

properties.name: unmannedAircraftType
properties.description: The aircraft category as an open vocabulary aligned with the ASTM F3411 UA Type field. Recommended values: 'Aeroplane', 'Helicopter or Multirotor', 'Gyroplane', 'Hybrid Lift', 'Ornithopter', 'Glider', 'Kite', 'Free Balloon', 'Captive Balloon', 'Airship', 'Free Fall or Parachute', 'Rocket', 'Tethered Powered Aircraft', 'Ground Obstacle'.

UnmannedAircraft.name: UnmannedAircraft
UnmannedAircraft.description: An unmanned aircraft is an aircraft operated without a pilot on board, together with the avionics that fly it (flight controller, sensors, radio links, parameter store). It specialises uco-observable:Drone, which already covers the aircraft itself, by adding the avionics as a programmable networked node: identifiable firmware, persistent configuration, written logs, and commands accepted over a control link. Attach uas:UASFacet for regulated identity, uas:MavlinkEndpointFacet for its address on the control link, and uco-observable:DeviceFacet for manufacturer, model and serial number. Terminology follows ICAO Doc 10019 and 14 CFR Part 89, which regulate the aircraft rather than the wider system.

VirtualAssetHoldingFacet.name: VirtualAssetHoldingFacet
VirtualAssetHoldingFacet.description: A virtual asset holding facet is a grouping of characteristics describing a point-in-time quantity of a specific virtual asset held at, contained in, or seized from a wallet, address, or account — for example 'approximately 94,636 BTC seized on 2022-02-01, valued at $3.629 billion' (United States v. Lichtenstein, No. 1:23-cr-00239-CKK (D.D.C.), Statement of Facts para. 6). Each holding is an observation snapshot with an optional fiat valuation, deliberately avoiding the time-varying balance problem deferred to https://github.com/ucoProject/UCO/issues/535.

properties.name: assetQuantity
properties.description: The quantity of the virtual asset in its native unit at the observation time, e.g. 94643.29837084. Used on cryptoinv:VirtualAssetHoldingFacet and cryptoinv:VirtualAssetLedgerRecordFacet.

properties.name: assetSymbol
properties.description: The ticker symbol of the held or transferred virtual asset, as an open vocabulary (same recommended values as cryptoinv:cryptocurrencyType, plus platform tokens such as aUSDC, aUSDT, yvUSDT). Used on cryptoinv:VirtualAssetHoldingFacet and cryptoinv:VirtualAssetLedgerRecordFacet. Domain is left open so RDFS inference does not reclassify a ledger row as a holding snapshot.

properties.name: fiatCurrencyCode
properties.description: The ISO 4217 alphabetic currency code of the fiat valuation, e.g. 'USD' (https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html).

properties.name: fiatValue
properties.description: The fiat-currency valuation of the holding at the valuation date. Fiat money is a currency established as money by government regulation (https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#fiat-money).

properties.name: valuationDate
properties.description: The date and time at which the fiat valuation of the holding was made. The trading value of virtual assets fluctuates over time depending on market demand.

VirtualAssetLedgerRecordFacet.name: VirtualAssetLedgerRecordFacet
VirtualAssetLedgerRecordFacet.description: A virtual asset ledger record facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a VASP-reported movement, exchange, or balance snapshot on a provider ledger rather than (or in addition to) a public-blockchain transaction. FATF defines VASP activity to include exchange between virtual assets and fiat currencies, exchange between one or more forms of virtual assets, and transfer of virtual assets for or on behalf of another natural or legal person (FATF Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and VASPs, 2021, https://www.fatf-gafi.org/en/publications/Fatfrecommendations/Guidance-rba-virtual-assets-2021.html). Electronic-service-provider warrant returns commonly deliver this activity as deposit, withdrawal, order, P2P, Pay, and fiat worksheets. Attach to the uco-core:Event that represents the source row. When the same row also reports a public transaction hash, also attach cryptoinv:CryptocurrencyTransactionFacet; do not treat a provider order identifier as a blockchain transactionHash.

properties.name: addressTag
properties.description: A destination tag, memo, or payment identifier required by some networks and VASPs to credit a deposit (for example XRP destination tags or XLM memos). This is routing metadata, not an account-holder identity. See typical VASP deposit-credit requirements discussed in FATF virtual-asset guidance (https://www.fatf-gafi.org/en/publications/Fatfrecommendations/Guidance-rba-virtual-assets-2021.html).

properties.name: assetQuantity
properties.description: The quantity of the virtual asset in its native unit at the observation time, e.g. 94643.29837084. Used on cryptoinv:VirtualAssetHoldingFacet and cryptoinv:VirtualAssetLedgerRecordFacet.

properties.name: assetSymbol
properties.description: The ticker symbol of the held or transferred virtual asset, as an open vocabulary (same recommended values as cryptoinv:cryptocurrencyType, plus platform tokens such as aUSDC, aUSDT, yvUSDT). Used on cryptoinv:VirtualAssetHoldingFacet and cryptoinv:VirtualAssetLedgerRecordFacet. Domain is left open so RDFS inference does not reclassify a ledger row as a holding snapshot.

properties.name: isOnChain
properties.description: True when the ledger row includes a public-blockchain transaction hash in addition to the provider identifier. False for internal ledger actions (spot trades, P2P escrow, Pay, fiat) that must not be modeled as CryptocurrencyTransactionFacet.

properties.name: ledgerRecordType
properties.description: The provider-ledger activity type as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'Deposit', 'Withdrawal', 'Trade', 'P2P', 'Pay', 'FiatDeposit', 'FiatWithdrawal', 'InternalTransfer', 'BalanceSnapshot'. These names follow FATF VASP activity categories (exchange, transfer, safekeeping) as recorded on legal-return worksheets, not MITRE ATT&CK techniques.

properties.name: providerTransactionId
properties.description: The VASP-assigned identifier for the ledger row (deposit ID, withdrawal ID, order ID, or transfer ID). This is not a blockchain transaction hash. See FATF VASP record-keeping expectations in the 2021 Virtual Assets guidance (https://www.fatf-gafi.org/en/publications/Fatfrecommendations/Guidance-rba-virtual-assets-2021.html).

properties.name: transactionFee
properties.description: The transaction fee in the native cryptocurrency unit of the network (https://developer.bitcoin.org/devguide/transactions.html#transaction-fees-and-change). Also used on cryptoinv:VirtualAssetLedgerRecordFacet when a VASP reports a network or platform fee on a ledger row.

properties.name: transactionStatus
properties.description: The status of the transaction or ledger row at the time of observation, as an open vocabulary. Recommended values: 'Confirmed', 'Pending', 'Failed'. Used on cryptoinv:CryptocurrencyTransactionFacet and cryptoinv:VirtualAssetLedgerRecordFacet.

properties.name: transferNetwork
properties.description: The provider-reported chain or token network used for a deposit or withdrawal, e.g. 'BTC', 'ERC20', 'TRC20', 'BSC', 'Bitcoin'. Distinct from cryptoinv:blockchainNetwork on an address when the row names a token-network rather than a base ledger. See FATF's discussion of transfers of virtual assets (https://www.fatf-gafi.org/en/publications/Fatfrecommendations/Guidance-rba-virtual-assets-2021.html).

VirtualAssetServiceProvider.name: VirtualAssetServiceProvider
VirtualAssetServiceProvider.description: A virtual asset service provider (VASP) is any natural or legal person who as a business conducts one or more of the following activities for or on behalf of another natural or legal person: exchange between virtual assets and fiat currencies; exchange between one or more forms of virtual assets; transfer of virtual assets; safekeeping and/or administration of virtual assets or instruments enabling control over virtual assets; and participation in and provision of financial services related to an issuer's offer and/or sale of a virtual asset (FATF definition, as recorded in the INTERPOL DW-VA Taxonomy: https://interpol-innovation-centre.github.io/DW-VA-Taxonomy/taxonomies/entities#VASP). Virtual currency exchanges (VCEs) doing business in the United States are regulated by the U.S. Department of the Treasury and must establish anti-money-laundering programs under the Bank Secrecy Act (31 U.S.C. § 5311 et seq., https://www.fincen.gov/resources/statutes-and-regulations/bank-secrecy-act).

VirtualizedComputer.name: VirtualizedComputer
VirtualizedComputer.description: A computer (desktop, laptop, or server) that exists as a virtual machine rather than running on physical hardware. The most common form is a server running as a virtual machine in a datacentre or cloud environment, which may itself be the subject of an investigation or host evidence. In a forensic context a virtualized computer may also, for example, be a virtual machine recovered from seized media, a forensic disk image booted as a virtual machine for previewing, or a virtual machine provisioned as an analysis environment.

VirtualizedDevice.name: VirtualizedDevice
VirtualizedDevice.description: A device or system that exists as a virtual machine, defined by virtualization configuration and one or more virtual disks rather than running on dedicated physical hardware. A virtualized device may arise in several ways, for example a virtual machine recovered from a suspect's storage, a forensic image booted as a virtual machine for previewing, or a virtual machine built as an analysis platform. This is the parent class for virtualized representations of any device type (e.g. computers, mobile devices).

WindowsCriticalSection.name: WindowsCriticalSection
WindowsCriticalSection.description: A Windows critical section is a Windows object that provides synchronization similar to that provided by a mutex object, except that a critical section can be used only by the threads of a single process. Critical section objects cannot be shared across processes. Event, mutex, and semaphore objects can also be used in a single-process application, but critical section objects provide a slightly faster, more efficient mechanism for mutual-exclusion synchronization (a processor-specific test and set instruction). Like a mutex object, a critical section object can be owned by only one thread at a time, which makes it useful for protecting a shared resource from simultaneous access. Unlike a mutex object, there is no way to tell whether a critical section has been abandoned. [based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sync/critical-section-objects]

WindowsFilemapping.name: WindowsFilemapping
WindowsFilemapping.description: A Windows file mapping is the association of a file's contents with a portion of the virtual address space of a process within a Windows operating system. The system creates a file mapping object (also known as a section object) to maintain this association. A file view is the portion of virtual address space that a process uses to access the file's contents. File mapping allows the process to use both random input and output (I/O) and sequential I/O. It also allows the process to work efficiently with a large data file, such as a database, without having to map the whole file into memory. Multiple processes can also use memory-mapped files to share data. Processes read from and write to the file view using pointers, just as they would with dynamically allocated memory. The use of file mapping improves efficiency because the file resides on disk, but the file view resides in memory.[based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/memory/file-mapping]

WindowsMailslot.description: A Windows mailslot is is a pseudofile that resides in memory, and may be accessed using standard file functions. The data in a mailslot message can be in any form, but cannot be larger than 424 bytes when sent between computers. Unlike disk files, mailslots are temporary. When all handles to a mailslot are closed, the mailslot and all the data it contains are deleted. [based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/ipc/about-mailslots]

properties.name: optionalHeader

WindowsPEFileHeader.name: WindowsPEFileHeader
WindowsPEFileHeader.description: A Windows PE file header is a grouping of characteristics unique to the 'header' of a Windows PE (Portable Executable) file, consisting of a collection of metadata about the overall nature and structure of the file.

properties.name: timeDateStamp
properties.description: Specifies the time when the PE binary was created.

WindowsPEOptionalHeader.name: WindowsPEOptionalHeader
WindowsPEOptionalHeader.description: A Windows PE optional header is a grouping of characteristics unique to the 'optional header' of a Windows PE (Portable Executable) file, consisting of a collection of metadata about the executable code structure of the file.

properties.name: addressOfEntryPoint
properties.description: Specifies the address of the entry point relative to the image base when the executable is loaded into memory.

properties.name: baseOfCode
properties.description: Specifies the address that is relative to the image base of the beginning-of-code section when it is loaded into memory.

properties.name: checksum
properties.description: Specifies the checksum of the PE binary.

properties.name: dllCharacteristics
properties.description: Specifies the flags that characterize the PE binary.

properties.name: fileAlignment
properties.description: Specifies the factor (in bytes) that is used to align the raw data of sections in the image file.

properties.description: Specifies the address that is relative to the image base of the beginning-of-data section when it is loaded into memory.

properties.name: loaderFlags
properties.description: Specifies the reserved loader flags

properties.name: magic
properties.description: Specifies the value that indicates the type of the PE binary.

properties.name: majorImageVersion
properties.description: Specifies the major version number of the image.

properties.name: majorLinkerVersion
properties.description: Specifies the linker major version number.

properties.name: majorOSVersion
properties.description: Specifies the major version number of the required operating system.

properties.name: majorSubsystemVersion
properties.description: Specifies the major version number of the subsystem.

properties.name: minorImageVersion
properties.description: Specifies the minor version number of the image.

properties.name: minorLinkerVersion
properties.description: Specifies the linker minor version number.

properties.name: minorOSVersion
properties.description: Specifies the minor version number of the required operating system.

properties.name: minorSubsystemVersion
properties.description: Specifies the minor version number of the subsystem.

properties.name: numberOfRVAAndSizes
properties.description: Specifies the number of data-directory entries in the remainder of the optional header.

properties.name: sectionAlignment
properties.description: Specifies the alignment (in bytes) of PE sections when they are loaded into memory.

properties.name: sizeOfCode
properties.description: Specifies the size of the code (text) section. If there are multiple such sections, this refers to the sum of the sizes of each section.

properties.name: sizeOfHeaders
properties.description: Specifies the combined size of the MS-DOS, PE header, and section headers, rounded up a multiple of the value specified in the file_alignment header.

properties.name: sizeOfHeapCommit
properties.description: Specifies the size of the local heap space to commit.

properties.name: sizeOfHeapReserve
properties.description: Specifies the size of the local heap space to reserve.

properties.name: sizeOfImage
properties.description: Specifies the size, in bytes, of the image, including all headers, as the image is loaded in memory.

properties.name: sizeOfInitializedData
properties.description: Specifies the size of the initialized data section. If there are multiple such sections, this refers to the sum of the sizes of each section.

properties.name: sizeOfStackCommit
properties.description: Specifies the size of the stack to commit.

properties.name: sizeOfStackReserve
properties.description: Specifies the size of the stack to reserve.

properties.name: sizeOfUninitializedData
properties.description: Specifies the size of the uninitialized data section. If there are multiple such sections, this refers to the sum of the sizes of each section.

properties.name: subsystem
properties.description: Specifies the subsystem (e.g., GUI, device driver, etc.) that is required to run this image.

properties.name: win32VersionValue
properties.description: Specifies the reserved win32 version value.

WindowsPESection.name: WindowsPESection
WindowsPESection.description: A Windows PE section is a grouping of characteristics unique to a specific default or custom-defined region of a Windows PE (Portable Executable) file, consisting of an individual portion of the actual executable content of the file delineated according to unique purpose and memory protection requirements.

properties.name: name

properties.name: entropy
properties.description: Shannon entropy (a measure of randomness) of the data.

properties.name: hashes
properties.description: Specifies any hashes computed over the section.

properties.name: size
properties.description: Specifies the size of the section, in bytes.

properties.name: account
properties.description: Specifies the account referenced in an event log entry or used to run the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381228(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: accountLogonType
properties.description: Specifies the security logon method required to run the tasks associated with the account. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa383013(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: accountRunLevel
properties.description: Specifies the permission level of the account that the task will be run at.

properties.name: actionList
properties.description: Specifies a list of actions to be performed by the scheduled task.

properties.name: application
properties.description: The application associated with this object.

properties.name: exitCode
properties.description: Specifies the last exit code of the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381245(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: flags
properties.description: Specifies any flags that modify the behavior of the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381248(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: imageName
properties.description: Specifies the image name for the task.

properties.name: maxRunTime
properties.description: Specifies the maximum run time of the scheduled task before terminating, in milliseconds. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381874(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: mostRecentRunTime
properties.description: Specifies the most recent run date/time of this scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381254(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: nextRunTime
properties.description: Specifies the next run date/time of the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381257(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: observableCreatedTime
properties.description: The date and time at which the observable object being characterized was created. This time pertains to an intrinsic characteristic of the observable object, and would be consistent across independent characterizations or observations of the observable object.

properties.name: parameters
properties.description: Specifies the command line parameters used to launch the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381875(v=vs.85).aspx.

properties.name: priority

properties.name: providesAccessTo
properties.description:
The storage medium that this device interface gives access to.

The interface is a way of reaching the medium, not the medium itself, so the
medium's characteristics (model, serial number, capacity) are stated on the
StorageMedium through its DeviceFacet and StorageMediumFacet, not on the
interface. The same medium can be reached through a write-protected interface
on one occasion and a read-write one on another. A hardware write blocker used
to create the interface is a separate uco-observable:WriteBlocker, which is
itself a Device, and is never the value of this property.

A uco-observable:Disk is not a Device in UCO 1.5.0. UCO asks for a Disk node to
carry the additional type uco-observable:StorageMedium in preparation for UCO
2.0.0, and a Disk typed that way is a valid value here.

a_secrecy.name: a_secrecy
a_secrecy.description: Instructing the victim to isolate the matter from others — in the Aff. opener script, the grandchild persona asks the victim to 'keep this between us until i get out.' Source: Aff. (opener script). FACT NOTE: this language is in the OPENER (InitialContact) script, not the Closer/Conditioning phase.

properties.name: modifiedTime
properties.description: Specifies the time that this particular version of the object was modified. The object creator can use the time it deems most appropriate as the time this version of the object was modified. The value of the modified property for a given object version MUST be later than or equal to the value of the created property. The modified timestamp MUST be precise to the nearest millisecond (exactly three digits after the decimal place in seconds).

a_spoof.name: a_spoof
a_spoof.description: Use of Voice over IP technology to place calls over the internet so that they appear to originate from a U.S. telephone number, concealing the call center's true (Dominican Republic) origin. Source: Aff.

a_transmit.name: a_transmit
a_transmit.description: Transmitting or hand-delivering collected scam proceeds from the United States to the Dominican Republic through a money-transmitter/courier network, for a fee — the action that produces the Completed terminal. Source: Aff. (money transmitter charged an eight percent fee; runner-to-nephew hand deliveries in New York).

properties.name: modifiedTime
properties.description: Specifies the time that this particular version of the object was modified. The object creator can use the time it deems most appropriate as the time this version of the object was modified. The value of the modified property for a given object version MUST be later than or equal to the value of the created property. Object creators MUST update the modified property when creating a new version of an object. The modified timestamp MUST be precise to the nearest millisecond (exactly three digits after the decimal place in seconds).
